entities.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
observations: In two direct human studies, high myocardial T2-weighted signal was positively associated with elevated high-sensitivity troponin T.
The association concerns T2-weighted signal and troponin T; it is distinct from late gadolinium enhancement or troponin I findings.

entities.name: HighT2-cTnT association
observations: In 101 outpatient HCM patients, elevated hs-cTnT (≥14 ng/L) occurred in 15/28 (54%) with high T2 signal versus 10/73 (14%) without high T2 signal (p<0.001). High-T2 extent correlated with hs-cTnT concentration (Spearman rho=0.42, p<0.001).

entities.name: T2-burden-cTnT trend
observations: In 44 HCM patients, increasing numbers of high-T2 segments were associated with higher hs-cTnT (Cochran-Armitage trend p=0.002); high-T2 myocardial percentage correlated with hs-cTnT (Pearson r=0.388, p=0.009).

entities.name: Exercise HighT2-cTnT
observations: In 127 HCM patients, high T2 signal was more frequent with post-exercise hs-cTnT rise (13/20, 65% vs 15/79, 19%; p<0.001) and independently predicted the rise (adjusted OR 7.9, 95% CI 2.7–23.3; p<0.001).
